dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ah sì? Di che tipo è la storia?
dialogue.translation: Oh really? What type of story is it?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: È un dramma, ma è interessante perché parla di una famiglia.
dialogue.translation: It's a drama, but it's interesting because it talks about a family.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Io invece ho letto un libro fantastico.
dialogue.translation: I, on the other hand, have read a fantastic book.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E di cosa parla?
dialogue.translation: And what is it about?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parla di un viaggio, ma la parte più bella è la fine.
dialogue.translation: It's about a trip, but the most beautiful part is the ending.

scenario: At a job interview (basic)

vocabulary.note: auxiliary and main verb, very frequent
masculine noun
feminine noun
regular verb in -are
feminine noun
adjective, also can be a noun
conjunction and interrogative adverb
interrogative adverb and conjunction
preposition, also can be an adverb
modal verb, irregular

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, signor Rossi. Allora, quanti anni ha?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, Mr. Rossi. So, how old are you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ho ventotto anni e ho tre anni di esperienza in questo settore.
dialogue.translation: I am twenty-eight years old and I have three years of experience in this sector.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bene. Parla qualche lingua straniera?
dialogue.translation: Good. Do you speak any foreign language?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sì, parlo francese e inglese, perché ho lavorato all'estero.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I speak French and English, because I have worked abroad.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quando può iniziare?
dialogue.translation: When can you start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Posso iniziare dopo due settimane, se vuole.
dialogue.translation: I can start after two weeks, if you want.

key_phrases.translation: Do you speak any foreign language?

scenario: Discussing food preferences at dinner
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Italian

vocabulary.note: Used with indirect pronouns (mi piace, ti piace) to express likes.
Regular verb in -are.
Feminine singular.
Can refer to the container or the food.
Generally placed after the noun.
Invariable, often placed before the word it modifies.
Can be an adverb or an indefinite pronoun.
Adverb of quantity.
As a noun, it means 'dessert'.
Irregular verb (bevo, bevi, beve...).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Che cosa ti piace mangiare a cena?
dialogue.translation: What do you like to eat for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mi piace il pesce, ma non troppo. Preferisco un piatto di pasta, è buono e leggero.
dialogue.translation: I like fish, but not too much. I prefer a plate of pasta, it's good and light.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Anche a me piace la pasta. Ma stasera ho mangiato poco, quindi prendo anche un dolce.
dialogue.translation: I also like pasta. But tonight I ate little, so I'll also have a dessert.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ottima idea! Cosa vuoi bere? Forse un vino rosso?
dialogue.translation: Great idea! What do you want to drink? Maybe a red wine?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sì, volentieri. Ma non troppo, perché dopo guido.
dialogue.translation: Yes, gladly. But not too much, because I'm driving afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Allora prendo anche io un po' di dolce e un caffè, così finiamo in bellezza.
dialogue.translation: Then I'll also have some dessert and a coffee, so we'll end on a high note.

key_phrases.translation: What do you like to eat?
I like... but not too much

scenario: Asking for help with a computer issue
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Italian

vocabulary.note: Used to open a program or a file.
To close a window or an application.
Irregular verb, past participle 'scritto'.
Web page or page of a document.
Often used for 'sito web'.
Agrees with the noun: veloce/veloci.
It can also mean 'so' (as in 'so much').
Attention: it's already on the avoidance list but here it's used as a natural conjunction.
As an adverb it means 'only'.
It can be followed by a past infinitive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Scusa, puoi aiutarmi? Non riesco ad aprire questa pagina sul sito.
dialogue.translation: Sorry, can you help me? I can't open this page on the site.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Certo. Che cosa succede? Forse è lento, o vedi un errore?
dialogue.translation: Sure. What's happening? Maybe it's slow, or do you see an error?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La pagina si apre, ma è molto lenta. E dopo non riesco a scrivere nulla.
dialogue.translation: The page opens, but it's very slow. And then I can't write anything.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Forse devi chiudere qualche programma. Così il computer va più veloce.
dialogue.translation: Maybe you should close some programs. That way the computer goes faster.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ho chiuso tutto, ma è ancora lento. Perché succede solo a me?
dialogue.translation: I closed everything, but it's still slow. Why does it happen only to me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Non preoccuparti. Dopo possiamo riavviare il computer, se vuoi.
dialogue.translation: Don't worry. Later we can restart the computer, if you want.

key_phrases.phrase: Non riesco ad aprire questa pagina

key_phrases.translation: Why does it happen only to me?

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Italian

vocabulary.note: Very frequent, means 'house' or 'dwelling'.
Often used for 'room' in the context of renting.
It can also be the verb 'affittare' (to rent).
Very common verb.
Often used with 'cercare'.
For telephoning.
Attention: it's already on the avoidance list, so don't use it. (I'll choose another verb)
Common adjective.
Can be an adjective or adverb.
Interrogative adverb of place.
Temporal adverb, very frequent.
Coordinating conjunction.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buongiorno, cerco una casa in affitto vicino all'università. Quando posso vederla?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I'm looking for a house for rent near the university. When can I see it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Abbiamo un appartamento libero, ma è un po' vecchio. La camera è grande.
dialogue.translation: We have a free apartment, but it's a bit old. The room is big.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Va bene. Dove si trova di preciso? Devo chiamare il proprietario?
dialogue.translation: Okay. Where exactly is it? Do I need to call the owner?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: È in via Roma, vicino alla fermata dell'autobus. Il proprietario è mio zio, posso dirgli tutto.
dialogue.translation: It's on Via Roma, near the bus stop. The owner is my uncle, I can tell him everything.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfetto. C'è anche un balcone? E quando posso trovare il contratto?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. Is there also a balcony? And when can I find the contract?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Certo, c'è un balcone nuovo. Se vuole, possiamo firmare subito.
dialogue.translation: Of course, there's a new balcony. If you want, we can sign right away.

key_phrases.translation: to look for a house for rent
